page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-2 is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel processor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1554.59 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1640.0. However, multi-core and memory subsystem performance are constrained. The multi-core CPU performance is rated poor with a stress-ng score of 1600.79 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2036.0. Memory bandwidth is also limited, measuring 15.05 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 9.22 GB/sec for large block write operations, both falling into the lower performance tier.

The n4-highmem-2 offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high computational throughput or local storage. Advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 are present, supporting specialized integer and cryptography operations. Given the weak multi-core scaling and poor database operation benchmarks, this instance is best suited for lightweight memory-optimized tasks, basic text processing, single-threaded applications, or small-scale web serving.

While it supports advanced instruction sets like Intel AMX and AVX-512, its computational and database performance is constrained. Consequently, the n4-highmem-2 is best suited for lightweight memory-intensive workloads, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and small-scale web serving where high memory capacity is prioritized over raw multi-core processing power.
